image_description: A museum exhibit featuring the fossilized skeleton of a Triceratops. The image focuses on the massive skull with its distinctive three horns and large bony frill, mounted on a metal armature. The rest of the skeletal structure (vertebrae, ribs, limbs) is visible in the background, along with other dinosaur skeletons and museum architecture (windows, ceiling).

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Three prominent horns: two long brow horns projecting forward and upward above the eyes, and a shorter nasal horn on the snout.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The fossil clearly displays the iconic triceratops horn configuration: two large supraorbital horns and one smaller nasal horn.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Beak is parrot-like with a sharp, keratinous cutting edge.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: This is a skeletal mount; the keratinous beak (soft tissue) is not preserved or present, only the underlying rostral bone is visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is quadrupedal with columnar, elephant-like limbs.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible limb bones (humerus, femur) are thick and columnar, consistent with the weight-bearing anatomy of a large quadruped.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Enormous bony frill (neck shield) extending posteriorly from the skull, with width dramatically exceeding the skull itself.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The parietal-squamosal frill is massive and clearly extends well beyond the width of the facial portion of the skull.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Frill is solid bone with a smooth outer surface and possible epoccipital (marginal) bumps.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The frill appears as solid bone (non-fenestrated) with visible texture consistent with fossilized bone surface.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is inferred to have been covered in large, hexagonal scales with possible quill-like structures along the back and tail.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: As a skeletal mount, no skin, scales, or soft tissue impressions are visible in this image.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Forelimbs are shorter than hindlimbs creating a sloping backline.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The mounting posture shows the characteristic ceratopsian stance where the shoulders are lower than the hips due to shorter forelimbs.
The caudal vertebrae visible in the background are thick and relatively short compared to the body length, matching the description.
